_note: WHERE A GRID SQUARE IS, FOR THE FEW PLACES HAMLET WILL SAY IT - work instruction 427, HM-DEC-180.
WHAT IT IS FOR. When a station's grid contradicts the entity his callsign prefix implies,
the grid wins (Tim, 2026-09-23): WL7E, an Alaska callsign, operating from CM98 in
California. To say that, Hamlet has to know which entity a grid square is in, and nothing
else in the tree does. This table is the whole of what it knows.
HOW A SQUARE IS PLACED. A four-character square is 2 degrees of longitude by 1 of latitude.
It is placed in a box only when the WHOLE square lies inside that box, and the first box
that holds it wins, so California is listed before the lower 48. A square that no box holds
whole is not placed at all, and the card says what it always said. A square on a border is
never placed: that is the case a grid cannot settle.
HOW THE BOXES WERE DRAWN. By the author of work instruction 427, from the known coordinates
of the borders - the 49th parallel, the Rio Grande, the Mexican border at 31.33 and 32.5 to
32.7 north, the California-Nevada line at 120 west north of 39 north, Cape Dezhnev at
169.65 west, Vancouver Island's southern tip at 48.3 north. Every piece of land inside a
box is in the named entity (and, for California, the named state); sea may be inside a box.
They are NOT read from a boundary file and no boundary file is in the tree. That is an
assumption, marked as one, and each box's reason says which border it keeps clear of.
THE WORD IS ENTITY. "entity" is the DXCC entity name exactly as
data/callsigns/dxcc-prefixes.json spells it; "place" is what the card says. DXCC counts
Alaska and Hawaii as entities apart from the lower 48.

places.why: Oregon is at 42 north; Nevada is east of 120 west from 39 north and further east below it; the rest is sea.
Mexico is south of 32.7 north and Arizona east of 114.6 west; the rest is sea.
Vancouver Island reaches south to 48.3 north, so the box stops at 48.
Canada is at 49 north here, and Lake Superior's Canadian shore and waters are north of 47; Mexico is south of 32.7.
Pelee Island, Canada, is at 41.7 north, so the box stops at 41; east of 72 west is New England's Canadian border and is left out.
The Rio Grande runs south of 30 north east of 104 west; west of 104 it is left out.
The Mexican border here is at 31.33 and 31.78 north.
The Rio Grande is at 29.6 north or south of it between 104 and 98 west.
The Rio Grande meets the sea at 25.9 north; the rest is the Gulf.
The Bahamas begin east of 79.3 west and Cuba south of 23.3 north.
Russia's Cape Dezhnev is at 169.65 west and the Yukon at 141 west; the panhandle south of 58 is left out.
Nothing but the islands and the sea.
